newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger but off early highs.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger but off early highs.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Friday, but fell from early highs as some traders took profits after the market rallied on a tame U.S. inflation report, analysts said.

"People just thought that was a good level to take profits and it's resulted in a bit of consolidation," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "From our viewpoint it was extremely heavy (trading)."
Canada's 30-year benchmark closed up C$0.25 to C$116.19 to yield 6.735 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond rose 17/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to zero from a negative spread of two basis points on Thursday. The Canada-U.S. 30-year spread on Thursday began trading negative for the first time in history.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the producer price index fell 0.3 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent rise. The report decreased expectations that the Federal Reserve would hike rates in July.
"The number really helped the market along. Basically no one thinks the Fed is going to raise rates in July and it's about 50/50 for August," said Dong. "There was a lot of fresh buying interest."
In new issue news, Precision Drilling Corp on Friday set C$200 million of 6.85 percent unsecured debentures due June 26, 2007 in financial markets, said lead manager RBC Dominion Securities Inc.
The bond was priced at 99.90 to yield 6.864 percent, 75 basis points over the Government of Canada's 7.25 percent bond due June 1, 2007.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.21 to C$107.83 to yield 6.184 percent, while the U.S. 10-year rose 13/32 to 6.43 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrrowed to 25 basis points from 27 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.82 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.97 percent.
